best_for: Malware analysts, CTF players and students who want a free graphical disassembler with a built-in decompiler, without paying for a commercial license.
description:
Cutter is a reverse engineering app from the Rizin project, the team behind the rizin framework. It takes compiled programs apart so you can see what they do, and the people who build it do this work themselves.

You can read code in a linear disassembly view, search a binary for byte patterns, define your own types and structs, and patch a file by adding, removing or changing bytes and instructions. A built-in rizin console takes typed commands when the menus are not enough. Pick a light, native, dark or midnight theme, or make your own in the theme editor.

points.title: A decompiler with no Java
points.text: Release builds include a native integration of Ghidra's decompiler, so you get C-like output next to the disassembly without installing Ghidra or a Java runtime.

points.title: Built on rizin
points.text: Cutter is the graphical front end for the rizin engine, which does the analysis. Version 2.5.0 uses rizin 0.9.1 and lets you view and edit rizin's configuration variables from a Preferences tab.

points.title: More than static analysis
points.text: You get a graph view with a mini-graph for navigation, a hex editor that can change files, emulation, and a native and remote debugger. The project still labels the debugger as beta.

points.title: Scriptable
points.text: Python scripts can automate tasks, and plugins can be written in Python or C++. An official and community plugin repository is linked from the project page.

points.title: Free under GPL-3.0
points.text: There are no paid tiers or accounts. The code is open source under GPL-3.0 and developed in the open on GitHub.

points.title: Linux here is a verified Flatpak
points.text: The Flatpak for x64 and Arm64 is marked verified on Flathub, so it comes from the Rizin Organization itself. The project also publishes an AppImage on GitHub.

points.title: Windows ships as a zip
points.text: The Windows build is an x64 zip with no installer; unpack it and run. The Windows listing keeps 6 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release, so downgrades there need another source.
